newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore calls tenders for more cellular licenses.
newsitem.headline: Singapore calls tenders for more cellular licenses.

text.p: Singapore said on Wednesday it will further liberalise its cellular mobile telephone services market and call for tenders later this year to award up to two more licenses from year 2000.

"The Telecommunications Authority of Singapore will be calling for tenders later this year to award up to two more cellular licences for provision of services from April 2000," Minister for Communications Mah Bow Tan said in a speech prepared for delivery to a business group.
The number of licenses awarded would depend on quality and attractiveness of tenders received, he said.
Foreign companies were welcome to team up with local players in bidding, with up to 49 percent direct foreign equity participation allowed.
Parties tendering for public basic telecommunication services (PBTS) licenses in Singapore were also invited to bid for the cellular licenses, Mah said.
"The time schedule of the cellular service tender has been synchronised with the PBTS main tender exercise" to allow for integrated network roll-out for players who may hold both licences, he said.
Tender results would be announced in mid-1998, giving successful licensees 18 months to get their networks ready.
Further details would be announced by the Telecommunication Authority of Singapore, Mah said.
Singapore has already authorised another cellular service provider in addition to Singapore Telecommunications Ltd, and is taking bids for up to two additional PBTS operators.
